findings.evidence: Lines 94–95 declare both instances section-wide; lines 103–241 consequently expose them on every theorem, while roadmap `Suggested.lean:249–257` states the canonical density and separation APIs using only the group topology/compactness assumptions.
findings.fix: Remove these two section-wide parameters and install `letI : MeasurableSpace G := borel G` locally where the Haar-based density proof is assembled; derive the remaining declarations from that measure-independent density theorem.
findings.issue: All ten declarations inherit `[MeasurableSpace G] [BorelSpace G]`, making density, separation, and representation faithfulness depend on caller-supplied measure data absent from their mathematical statements and the roadmap signature.

summary: The public Peter–Weyl API unnecessarily exposes an auxiliary measurable-space choice, although every theorem is topological and Haar measure can use the canonical Borel structure internally.
